decisions: Treat Binance's 90% replenishment and 100% top-ten coverage, including XRP, as company-reported claims pending the full November 3 zero-knowledge proof.
Do not infer an XRP-specific replacement purchase from Binance's remaining 10%; Binance says that remainder is outside the top ten and less liquid.
Treat the reported 7,500 BTC SAFU movement as a reserve transfer/reallocation with unknown destination and purpose; do not classify it as a market sale or XRP purchase.
Prefer fresh Arkham and Lookonchain evidence for the SAFU source-wallet balance while retaining BitInfoCharts' 15,000 BTC result as a stale conflicting observation.

Downgrade the hypothesis that Binance suffered a persistent 220M XRP reserve depletion caused by the incident; XRP Insights' Oct 31 same-wallet rebound and Binance 7d/30d changes are disconfirming, but provider wallet universes still differ.
Treat broad exchange-attributed XRP balances as custody/reserve context, not tradable float; explicitly remove Binance-Peg and cbXRP backing reserves from customer/available-float interpretations.
Do not admit SAFU transfers or exchange wallet totals as directional prediction features without point-in-time reconciliation and out-of-sample validation.
required_verification: Find the 7,500 BTC transaction hash and destination address using public on-chain explorers/authorized APIs.
Trace destination wallet balances and subsequent transfers to determine whether BTC was retained, exchanged, sent OTC or moved internally.
Verify the November 3 full Binance PoR zero-knowledge proof and compare same-time XRP customer liabilities and reserve addresses.
Crosswalk Binance XRP wallets between CryptoQuant and XRP Insights; isolate customer, cold, Binance-Peg and operational balances.
Verify Binance withdrawal reopening on November 1 and any subsequent official status.
